transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well... I suppose I'm here because I've been noticing a pattern for months now. 

It's just... things like my sister's appointments getting moved around, or bills showing up wrong. People suddenly forgetting to call me back. Everyone keeps telling me they're just mistakes, but... I know they're keeping information from me. They're trying to push me out of decisions.

When you say they're keeping information from you and trying to push you out of decisions—do you believe this is intentionally coordinated against you, or do you think these are just coincidences and mistakes?

I thought I just said that. Everyone else calls them mistakes, but... I don't. You don't have that many coincidences happen for months on end. They are doing it on purpose so I don't have a say in anything.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things, or experienced anything through your senses that others around you couldn't perceive or didn't seem to notice?
No. Nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... see things. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. It's just the things that are actually happening that I'm talking about.

Besides people keeping information from you and pushing you out of decisions, do you believe other things are happening to you—like people following you, your thoughts being controlled, or anything else that feels intentional and directed at you?
No. I haven't noticed anything like that. Just... what I already told you.

When someone you trust—like a family member or close friend—explains to you that these things are actually just coincidences or mistakes, does any part of you start to doubt your belief, or do you remain completely convinced that they're intentionally coordinating against you?

I don't doubt it. I know what I'm seeing. My sister's appointments get moved around, bills show up wrong, people conveniently forget to call me back... it's a pattern. Even when everyone else tells me it's just mistakes, I know they're keeping information from me. They want me out of the picture. I'm completely convinced.

How much of your day do you spend thinking about these patterns and what people are doing to keep information from you? Has this affected your ability to work, maintain relationships, or do daily activities?

I don't... I don't spend all day on it. Just when I'm dealing with my sister's appointments and trying to get straight answers. 

Outside of that, I still do my job. I supervise my staff, I pay my bills, my house is in order. I know some people might think I'm... too focused on this whole thing, but I'm not falling apart. I'm not acting strangely in other parts of my life. Everything else is fine.

Besides people keeping information from you about your sister's appointments and decisions, do you have beliefs about other areas of your life—like your health, your finances beyond the bills you mentioned, or your safety—where you think something intentional is happening to you?
No. I... no. My health is fine. And I'm perfectly safe. It's really just... what I already told you. Just the situation with my sister. That's all.

If I were to sit down with your sister and some of these other people involved, and they showed you documentation or evidence that these things really were just coincidences or mistakes—like showing you that appointment changes happened due to a scheduling system glitch, or that bills were corrected automatically—would that change your mind about what's happening, or would you still believe they're coordinating against you?

I... no. I don't think so. 

Like I said, I've been seeing this exact same pattern for months now. The appointments getting moved, the bills showing up wrong, people conveniently forgetting to call me back. They can show me whatever papers they want and tell me they're just mistakes. But I know they're keeping information from me. They're just trying to push me out of the decisions. 

So... no. It wouldn't change my mind.
